A1.justification: Both PDFs identify arXiv 2502.03771 and retain the semantic caching problem and classification benchmark, despite substantial method revision and retitling. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original cache-hit, error-rate, latency, and sampling-ablation results in Section 6 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v3 reports original caching performance, error-bound compliance, and latency experiments across classification, chatbot, and search-query benchmarks in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: VectorQ's three threshold regions, normalized correctness posterior, and uncertainty gate are replaced by vCache's online sigmoid correctness model and confidence-based exploration policy controlled by a maximum error tolerance δ. This changes the decision procedure, not merely its name. v3 also introduces LLM-judge response-equivalence checking for longer responses.

E1.justification: The earlier 45,000-prompt Semantic Prompt Caching Benchmark is retained as SemCacheClassification, with the same three source datasets and listed label counts. v3 additionally evaluates 60,000 LMArena-derived prompts, including generated paraphrases, and 150,000 ORCAS-derived search queries. These substantially extend coverage beyond fixed-label classification to chatbot and search scenarios.

E2.justification: The static-threshold comparator is retained as GPTCache. v3 Figures 4–5 add GPTCache with embeddings fine-tuned using Zhu et al.'s method and evaluate vCache with those embeddings; v2 only discussed such fine-tuning as a possible mitigation. The uniform-sampling comparator from v2 Figure 18 is removed with its ablation.

E3.justification: v2's four GTE/E5-Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B/70B combinations are replaced by plotted GTE/Llama-3.1-8B and E5-large-v2/GPT-4o-mini evaluations. Reported hardware changes from A100 to B200. v3 introduces δ sweeps, ROC and average-latency reporting, and equivalence-class scoring for new benchmarks, whereas v2 relied on character matching. These are revised or additional protocols.

E4.justification: v2's correctness-versus-uniform sampling ablation, controlled cache-hit/miss overhead experiment, and cache-size latency regression disappear. v3 adds error-bound compliance and learning curves over increasing sample sizes, plus embedding-generation overhead analysis. The threshold-dilemma analysis changes from two individual embedding distributions to aggregate distributions and a histogram of learned thresholds.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D reports confidence intervals obtained from three evaluations per uncertainty-gate configuration. v3 Section 5 instead specifies 95% intervals using Wallis binomial confidence bounds, without retaining the three-repeat disclosure. This changes uncertainty estimation and reporting; it does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Substantial result sets are replaced or added. v2 reports up to 26× higher cache-hit rates and 74% lower error; v3 reports up to 2× higher hit rates and 6× lower error on LMArena, under different evaluations. v3 additionally reports below-target errors but acknowledges static-cache advantages on the 150,000-query search Pareto comparison. v2's standalone Amazon/Ecommerce result panels are removed.

T1.justification: v2's threshold-convergence argument and simplified posterior-convergence analysis are replaced by a formal user-guarantee definition, sigmoid likelihood model, confidence-bound derivations, Theorem 4.1, and Lemmas B.1–B.2. The claimed guarantee concerns correctness for arbitrary prompts and sample sizes under i.i.d. and correctly specified sigmoid assumptions, substantially changing both the theoretical target and assumptions.

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from adaptive threshold regions with convergence to the first verified semantic cache enforcing a user-defined error bound. Error-rate guarantees were explicitly future work in v2 Section 6.3. v3 also claims robustness to out-of-distribution inputs, extends comparisons to fine-tuned embeddings, and makes three benchmark releases a principal contribution.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes exact-match rigidity and embedding-domain or language mismatch. v3 discusses LLM-judge overhead and failure of its analysis when i.i.d. or sigmoid assumptions fail. It attributes conservative small-δ performance to uncertainty and argues that increasing static-cache error supports vCache's long-term reliability, including where finite-sample comparisons favor GPTCache.

D1.justification: v3 adds implementation and benchmark access links and substantial construction details, including LMArena paraphrase generation and ORCAS clustering with LLM-judged equivalence classes. It documents B200 hardware and the experimental use of confidence bounds only for the threshold, with a point estimate for sigmoid slope. v2's temperature-zero and vLLM memory-utilization disclosures are no longer provided.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from semantic caches and complementary KV-caching engines to embedding fine-tuning, threshold optimization, and correctness guarantees. v3 develops comparisons with Zhu et al., threshold-consistent margin learning, and Rudd et al.'s Extreme Value Machine, while removing the vLLM/SGLang discussion. This substantially revises the novelty argument and research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. The long region-construction example is replaced by an overview and guarantee/model/policy organization; threshold motivation moves partly into Appendix C.3, limitations become a separate section, and appendices are reorganized. The title, method terminology, and author presentation also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Region-evolution and architecture diagrams are replaced by decision-boundary and probability illustrations, while result grids become learning-curve and ROC/Pareto displays. New benchmark histograms are added, and v2's separate and combined label-distribution tables are consolidated into v3 Table 1.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical relevance through chatbot/search evaluations, fine-tuned baselines, and additional reproducibility information. However, error guarantees move from future work in v2 to the central claim without secure support as written: Appendix B, Eq. 20 assumes the sigmoid increases with slope gamma at every similarity, although it decreases below the threshold. The appendix also states that experiments omit uncertainty in gamma. These gaps in the new headline guarantee make the net quality effect uncertain despite the empirical gains.
